title: The Lost Key

full_text:
Late one moonlit evening, several neighbors walking through the town square noticed Mulla Nasruddin down on all fours in the dust beneath a bright street lamp, searching frantically for something.

"What have you lost, Mulla?" asked a friendly neighbor, kneeling down to help him sift through the gravel.

"I have lost the iron key to my front door," replied Nasruddin, wiping sweat from his brow.

The neighbors immediately joined the search. For nearly an hour, five men crawled upon their hands and knees, combing through every pebble beneath the lamp, but not a trace of the key could be found.

Exhausted, one of the neighbors asked: "Mulla, are you absolutely sure you dropped the key here in the square?"

"Oh, no!" answered Nasruddin casually, pointing toward the dark alleyway twenty yards away. "I dropped it inside the dark coal-cellar behind my house!"

The neighbors stared at him in utter disbelief: "Then why in heaven's name are you searching for it out here under the street lamp?"

"Can you not see?" laughed Nasruddin with wide-eyed innocence. "It is pitch black in my cellar, whereas out here under the street lamp, there is plenty of light to see!"

The neighbors groaned, but Sufi masters smiled, knowing Nasruddin had just illustrated how mortals seek truth in the superficial glitter of the world rather than searching the deep, dark caverns of their own hearts.
moral: Searching for answers where it is convenient rather than where the truth was lost is human folly.
